task: 4. Define shared install and model provenance manifests
commit_subject: build: define install and model manifests

model_manifest.note: Model sha256 values are the real deployed file hashes (computed from var/lib/namtor/models/, gitignored). licence_sha256 values are SPDX-canonical licence-text hashes. Signature verification (GPG/cosign over the manifest) is task 6; this task defines the manifest format and daemon-side sha256+licence+redistribution validation.

staging_determinism.method: Ran packaging/stage.sh twice from a stub SRCDIR (real packaging/ files + stub target/release/ binaries) into two empty DESTDIRs. Compared the resulting trees by (type, mode, relative-path, content-sha256|symlink-target).
staging_determinism.script: packaging/stage.sh (python3 stdlib tomllib parser; deterministic: sorted entries, no timestamp preservation, explicit modes)
staging_determinism.verdict: DETERMINISTIC — two stagings into empty roots produce identical file trees (same paths, modes, content sha256).
staging_determinism.caveat: Run as non-root in this evidence pass, so owner/group were not applied (script warns). Modes and content — the deterministic properties — are identical. Root-run staging additionally applies owner/group by name; ownership determinism follows from the manifest declaring owner/group for every entry.

cases.notes: valid offline cache: file present + sha256 match + licence.accepted present → proceeds without network
on-disk sha256 != manifest sha256 → 'tampered model ... sha256 mismatch'
no licence.accepted record, NAMTOR_ACCEPT_LICENCE unset → 'licence not accepted'
policy=restricted, allow_restricted=false → 'restricted model ... requires explicit authorisation'
spec.id not in manifest → 'not present in manifest'
manifest has fp32 only, spec asks int8 → 'no Int8 variant'
real packaging/model-manifest.toml parses; ids=[yunet_2023mar, sface_2021dec, minifasnet_pad]; each has fp32 variant + licence_sha256
hex codec for 32-byte sha256 round-trips; rejects short/non-hex

model_manifest_gate_tests.summary: 9/9 model-manifest tests pass. Tampered / unaccepted / restricted each block startup (fail closed). Valid offline cache proceeds. The committed packaging/model-manifest.toml parses and lists the three deployed models with their real sha256 + tensor contracts + licence hashes.

verification.cargo_test: cargo test -p namtor-daemon --lib -- --skip concurrent_connections_serialise --test-threads=1 → 64 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored
verification.note: Pre-existing flake listener::concurrent_connections_serialise_on_camera_lock skipped per learnings.md; pre-existing env-var races in licence::tests avoided via --test-threads=1.

dependencies_added.justification: Manifest parsing is a core daemon function. toml 0.8 already a direct dep in namtor-hwdb/namtor-probe/namtor-camera; no new transitive weight (toml_edit already in the workspace graph via those crates).

out_of_scope: GPG/cosign signature verification of model-manifest.toml — task 6 (signed packages). This task defines the manifest fields required for signing (sha256, licence_sha256) and the daemon-side sha256+licence+redistribution validation; it does not implement signature verification.

Wiring validate_against_manifest into the daemon binary entry point (crates/namtor-daemon/src/bin/namtor-daemon.rs) — outside the allowed file set for this task. The function is public and ready to call; the bin currently hardcodes [0;32] sha256 and does not consult the manifest. Wiring is a follow-up that belongs with the daemon-startup integration task.

INT8 variants for the deployed models — R4 (INT8 vs FP32) is WITHHELD per docs/evidence/status-audit.md (Path B). The manifest schema supports multiple variants per model_id; INT8 rows are added when R4 lands.
